key_insight: Long-range ML interatomic potentials better capture electrostatic defect interactions in SrTiO3 than short-range models, especially for vacancy-pair energetics and migration barriers.
engineering_relevance: Accurate long-range force fields can improve defect-transport predictions in oxides, supporting more reliable materials design for electronic, ionic, and defect-engineering applications.
method: Benchmarked MACE-POLAR, MACE-LES, and LOREM against short-range MACE.
Started with synthetic point-charge tests, then moved to first-principles SrTiO3 defect data.
Evaluated Sr–O Schottky vacancy pairs and oxygen-vacancy migration using CI-NEB and MD.
evidence_signal: The paper compares model performance across idealized electrostatics and realistic DFT crystal-defect datasets, using vacancy-pair separation dependence and migration barriers as the main evaluation signals.
watch_item: Results may still depend on how well long-range effects are represented in DFT training data, since total energies mix Coulombic interactions with screening and exchange-correlation contributions.
paper_title: Long-Range Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials for Defect Energetics in SrTiO$_3$
